batch_notes: The batch contains one id three times: rust/slotmap::hegel_removed_key_invalid_after_heavy_slot_reuse appears in basic.rs, dense.rs and hop.rs with the same id; I emitted one entry per occurrence in batch order (all classified identically) so the count matches 139. Recurring shapes: (1) 'Expected failure: <bug>' properties in rust/size and 'sprintf/N:' properties in rust/sprintf are the bug's own recorded test, yet most are narrowed generators around one failure (tagged pin where the generator is confined to the failing region); the general differential (floats_match_libc, integers_match_libc) gates around them with tc.assume, and the README of sprintf/15 says the differential found it even though the record names the pin property. (2) std containers used as models: following batch-09, Vec's own same-named ops as the reference for SmallVec were tagged oracle:external, while BTreeMap/HashMap used as an abstract model of sled/slotmap/spade were tagged oracle:model. (3) rust/shlex::doc_examples is a fixed-example test under a hegel attribute (other, as in batch-13). (4) rust/sled and rust/smallvec have no doc comments at all; classification is from bodies. (5) The rubric has no clean home for 'iterator/drain schedule against a model' single-object tests; I used stateful-model when the schedule is checked step by step (sled double-ended iteration, pop_in_range) and external-oracle plus a stateful tag when the sequence is against Vec (smallvec into_iter, truncate/resize).
